observation: The outermost silhouette of the head and hair must read as one continuous closed loop even where individual hair wisps break the edge
reason: An open outer border lets the background fill leak into the subject and ruins the whole page
possible_rule: Force-close the single outermost contour before region detection; bridge silhouette gaps under a small pixel radius

observation: The body outline nearly disappears where similar-tone fur meets a similar-tone background; the edge drops to very low contrast
reason: Low-contrast silhouette segments vanish during global thresholding and open the outer border
possible_rule: Use a contrast-adaptive threshold along the outer silhouette and never drop the longest boundary loop

observation: A clean product edge on a plain background is high-contrast and closes easily, but soft drop-shadow blurs the true edge
reason: Shadow gradients can be mistaken for the border and push it outward
possible_rule: Anchor the outer border to the highest-gradient ring, not to the shadow falloff

observation: The face-to-neck boundary is defined by a soft cast shadow rather than a hard drawn line
reason: Soft tonal transitions create weak or broken inner borders that fail to enclose the neck
possible_rule: Promote long soft-shadow edges to closed inner borders when they separate distinct tonal planes

observation: Where the handle meets the body the inner border must fully separate the two fill areas at the join
reason: A missing join border merges handle and body into one leaking region
possible_rule: Guarantee T-junction borders close so both meeting regions stay independently enclosed

observation: The hairline is a ragged fringe of many small strands rather than a single clean curve
reason: Treating every strand as a border creates dozens of tiny leaking regions along the fringe
possible_rule: Collapse the hairline fringe into one smoothed boundary and keep only strands above a length/contrast threshold

observation: The outer fur edge is fuzzy and individual hairs cross the silhouette line
reason: Fuzzy edges produce jagged non-closing outer borders that leak into the background
possible_rule: Smooth the outer fur silhouette into a closed curve while preserving interior strand strokes

observation: Stripes are hard-edged internal borders that must remain separate from the base fur regions
reason: Merging stripes into the fur flattens the animal's identity and loses the pattern
possible_rule: Preserve high-contrast internal band borders as their own closed regions

observation: The eye is a set of nested closed borders: eyelid, sclera, iris, pupil, plus a small highlight dot
reason: Broken nested rings cause eye parts to merge and the gaze/expression to collapse
possible_rule: Guarantee each concentric eye ring closes; keep the catchlight as its own tiny closed region if above minimum area

observation: The upper eyelid crease is a fine faint line that easily breaks into segments
reason: A broken crease opens the eye-socket region and lets skin fill flood the eye
possible_rule: Bridge sub-3px gaps on facial feature lines before flood fill

observation: The animal pupil (round or slit) is a strong high-contrast closed shape
reason: Losing the pupil border removes a defining feature of the face
possible_rule: Retain the highest-contrast small closed shapes inside the eye region

observation: The lip border is defined more by a color and tone change than by any drawn line
reason: Color-defined borders are missed by pure edge detection and never close
possible_rule: Reinforce the lip boundary using tonal-plane separation, then close it into a region

observation: Nostrils are small dark closed shapes that must not merge into the surrounding nose
reason: Merged nostrils flatten the nose form and look wrong
possible_rule: Keep small high-contrast dark shapes as separate closed regions when above minimum area

observation: The nose pad (leather) has a distinct closed outline separating it from the muzzle fur
reason: An open nose boundary lets muzzle fill leak into the nose pad
possible_rule: Close the nose-pad contour and treat it as a priority outline

observation: The cheek and jaw are smooth organic arcs and must not become polygonal after simplification
reason: Over-simplification turns faces angular and off-model, destroying likeness
possible_rule: Fit smooth curves to long organic contours and cap corner insertion below a curvature threshold

observation: The ear outer curve is a smooth sweep ending in a rounded tip
reason: Jagged or faceted ear edges read as low quality
possible_rule: Preserve curvature continuity along the ear contour with no visible stair-stepping

observation: Petal edges are gently curved with soft tips and overlap neighboring petals
reason: Angular petals break the floral identity and overlaps must still separate
possible_rule: Smooth petal boundaries while keeping each petal-to-petal overlap border closed

observation: Some interior regions fail to close where two soft edges nearly meet but leave a 1-2px gap
reason: Near-miss gaps are the single biggest cause of fill leaks across regions
possible_rule: Run a gap-close pass that bridges stroke endpoints within a small radius before flood fill

observation: Glasses frames are thin closed loops that must enclose the lens regions
reason: Thin frames drop out under thresholding and open the lens region
possible_rule: Thicken thin structural loops just enough to guarantee closure without distorting the shape

observation: Where one object overlaps another, the occluding edge must close the front shape and cut the back shape
reason: A missing occlusion border merges foreground and background objects into one region
possible_rule: Give occluding contours border priority and ensure both shapes remain closed

observation: Diagonal and curved borders show pixel stair-stepping after thresholding
reason: Aliased borders look unprofessional and confuse downstream smoothing and SVG export
possible_rule: Threshold with sub-pixel awareness and smooth stair-steps that fall under a curvature threshold

observation: Jagged control is needed on the outer fur edge but interior strand detail must be kept sharp
reason: Global smoothing erases meaningful strands while no smoothing leaves outer jaggies
possible_rule: Apply stronger smoothing to the outer silhouette than to interior strokes

observation: Skin shows fine grain and pores that are not real borders
reason: Grain becomes speckle regions and false borders that clutter the face
possible_rule: Suppress low-contrast short non-closing edges (texture) before region detection

observation: Dense fur micro-texture produces thousands of tiny edges where only flow-aligned strokes carry meaning
reason: Micro-texture explodes the region count and hides the real structure and stripes
possible_rule: Keep only long directional higher-contrast strokes and drop isolated flecks

observation: Some real structural borders are faint and risk being deleted along with the noise
reason: Aggressive noise removal can destroy true low-contrast outlines and open large regions
possible_rule: Protect any edge that contributes to closing a large region even if faint (closure-weighted keep)
